lessons.name: File-based Routing
lessons.desc: page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx, not-found.tsx — what each file does and when it renders
terms: URL ka pattern jo batata hai kaunsa page khulega — /about, /blog/meri-post.
app/ folder ke folders hi routes ban jaate hain — alag se routing config nahi likhna padta.
Us URL par kya DIKHEGA — bina is file ke folder route nahi banta.
lessons.what:
Next.js mein routing folders se banti hai. app/users/page.tsx likha to /users URL apne aap ban gaya.

Koi route config nahi, koi react-router nahi — folder ka naam hi URL hai.
lessons.analogy: Ghar ke kamre — darwaze par naam ka plate laga hai. Plate = folder ka naam (URL), kamre ka saaman = page.tsx. Naam plate dekh kar mehmaan seedha kamre tak pahunch jaata hai.
lessons.why: Pehle har project ka apna routing config hota tha — har jagah alag style. File-based routing ne ek convention di: sab projects ka structure same dikhta hai, naya developer bhi turant samajh jaata hai ki kaunsa page kahan hai.

lessons.code:
app/
├── page.tsx              → /
├── about/page.tsx        → /about
├── blog/
│   ├── page.tsx          → /blog          (list)
│   └── [slug]/page.tsx   → /blog/kuch-bhi (detail)
└── components/Header.tsx → KOI ROUTE NAHI ✓

// page.tsx ke bina folder sirf folder hai:
app/users/layout.tsx    // route NAHI bana
app/users/page.tsx      // ab /users ban gaya

// Special files ka kaam:
layout.tsx   // aas-paas ka dancha (persist hota hai)
loading.tsx  // chalte waqt ka fallback
error.tsx    // girne par ka fallback
where: Pages, blogs, dashboards — sab kuch isi se banta hai.
Component files ko route folder ke andar rakh sakte ho — wo route nahi bante.
"App Router vs Pages Router" ka pehla farak yahi hai — config vs convention.
pros: Zero config — folder banao, route ready.
Structure dekh kar hi poora site samajh aata hai.
Private files (_folder) aur groups jaise tools built-in.
cons: Folder naam hi URL hai — rename karna matlab URLs badalna.
Deep nesting se paths lambe ho jaate hain.
Naye log "components folder kyu route nahi bana?" par atak jaate hain.
gotchas: page.tsx ke bina folder route nahi banta — sabse common beginner confusion.
components/ ya lib/ jaise folders ke andar ki files routes nahi banti — sirf special files (page, layout...) matter karti hain.
Ek hi folder mein page.tsx aur route.ts saath nahi reh sakte — build error.

lessons.name: Layouts & Templates
lessons.desc: Persistent layouts vs. re-mounting templates. Root layout, nested layouts, layout composition
terms: Aas-paas ka dancha jo navigation par wahi rehta hai — state preserve hoti hai, re-render nahi hota.
Layout jaisa hi, par har navigation par naya mount hota hai — purani state mit jaati hai.
app/layout.tsx — zaroori hai, isi mein <html> aur <body> tags likhe jaate hain.
lessons.what:
layout.tsx apne saare child pages ko wrap karta hai aur navigation ke dauran zinda rehta hai — sidebar wapas render nahi hota, uski state bani rehti hai.

template.tsx bilkul same kaam karta hai, bas har navigation par naya instance banta hai.
lessons.analogy: Office building — deewarein, lift, lobby (layout) kabhi nahi badalte; kamre ke andar ka furniture (template) har tenant ke saath badal jaata hai.
lessons.why: Pehle har navigation par poora page dobara render hota tha — sidebar flicker karta tha, scroll position chali jaati thi. Layouts ne persistent shell diya: sirf andar ka hissa badalta hai.

visual.cap: Navigation par layout apni jagah rehta hai, sirf children badalte hain. Template hota to poora remount hota.

where: Auth state, cart count — ye layouts mein rehte hain taaki navigation par na udein.
Dashboard ka apna sidebar, blog ka apna header — nested layouts se.
Page enter animation chahiye har navigation par? Layout nahi, template.tsx.
pros: State preserve — input bhara hua, scroll position, video playback sab bach jaata hai.
Nested layouts se complex shells bina prop drilling ke.
Layout mein data fetch karke children ko pass kar sakte ho.
cons: Layout kabhi unload nahi hota — usme galat state rakhi to poori app affected.
Template vs layout ka farak shuru mein confusing.
Root layout mein html/body na ho to build fail.
gotchas: Root layout mein <html> aur <body> tags likhna ZAROORI hai — warna hydration error.
Layout ke andar useState navigation par reset NAHI hota — ye feature hai, bug nahi.
Templates mein useEffect har navigation par dobara chalta hai — kabhi kabhi yahi chahiye hota hai.

lessons.name: Dynamic Routes
lessons.desc: [slug], [...slug], [[...slug]] — catch-all, optional catch-all, generateStaticParams for SSG
terms: Dynamic segment — URL ka wo hissa jo badal sakta hai.
Ek se zyada segments pakadta hai — /docs/a/b/c.
Build time par batata hai kaunse slug pages pehle se ban jaayein (SSG).
lessons.what:
[slug] folder ka naam URL mein kisi bhi value se replace ho jaata hai. app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx — /blog/react, /blog/css dono isi se chalte hain.

Page ko wo value params prop mein milti hai.
lessons.analogy: Speed post ka address slip — pattern same rehta hai, bas naam-gali ki jagah (slug) har envelope par alag likha hota hai. Ek hi slip ka format, lakhon addresses.
lessons.why: 1000 blog posts ke liye 1000 folders? Nahi. Ek dynamic route + database = sab posts ek hi file se. Isi cheez ko REST ka :id jaisa socho, par folders mein.

where: Har post/product ka apna URL — ek hi file se.
generateStaticParams se sab posts build time par static.
pros: Unlimited pages ek file se.
Static generation ke saath mil kar bahut tez.
Catch-all se flexible URL structures.
cons: Galat slug ka handling khud likhna padta hai (notFound()).
Params ka Promise hona (Next 15) purane tutorials todta hai.
Bahut saare dynamic params se build slow ho sakti hai.
gotchas: Next.js 15 mein params ek Promise hai — await params karna zaroori. Purana params.slug silently galat chal sakta hai.
[...slug] khaali URL (/docs) match nahi karta — uske liye [[...slug]] chahiye.
Invalid slug par notFound() call karna bhool jaao to user ko khaali page milta hai.

lessons.name: Loading & Error UI
lessons.desc: Streaming with loading.tsx, error.tsx boundaries, global-error.tsx, reset() function
terms: Us route ke data aate tak ka turant fallback — Suspense boundary apne aap ban jaata hai.
Render fail hone par ka fallback — ErrorBoundary + reset() retry button.
notFound() call hone par ya galat URL par ka 404 UI.
lessons.what:
Ye teeno special files route ke error/loading states sambhalti hain — bina ek line state management ke.

loading.tsx daala to data aate tak wahan skeleton dikhta hai; error.tsx daala to crash hone par graceful message + retry.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant — order dete hi starter aa jaata hai (loading.tsx). Dish bigad jaaye to manager aata hai maafi ke saath aur fresh order dilwaata hai (error.tsx). Jo menu mein hi nahi wo "not available" card (not-found.tsx).
lessons.why: Server components async hain — data aane mein time lagta hai, aur kahin na kahin fail ho sakta hai. In files ke bina har page mein khud loading/error state likhna padta. Next ne convention bana diya.

where: Slow queries par skeletons — page white nahi dikhta.
error.tsx se retry UX bina extra library ke.
Invalid id par notFound() — proper 404 SEO ke saath.
pros: Zero boilerplate — file daalo, state management free.
Error isolation — ek widget gire, poora page nahi.
reset() se bina reload ke retry.
cons: error.tsx client component banana padta hai.
Production mein error.message redacted hota hai — debug karna alag se.
Nested routes mein kaunsa boundary pakdega, track karna padta hai.
gotchas: error.tsx mein 'use client' likhna zaroori hai — warna build error.
Error upar bubble hota hai — nearest parent error.tsx use pakadta hai, wahi nahi jisne throw kiya.
global-error.tsx root layout ko replace karta hai — ismein <html><body> khud likhne padte hain.

lessons.name: Metadata API
lessons.desc: Static metadata export, generateMetadata(), Open Graph, Twitter cards, robots, sitemap, viewport
terms: Page ke <head> mein jaane wali info — title, description, OG image.
Dynamic metadata — URL/data ke hisaab se har page ka apna title.
WhatsApp/Twitter par link share hone par dikhne wali preview card.
lessons.what:
Next.js mein SEO tags likhne ke liye bas ek metadata object export kar do — framework use <head> mein daal deta hai.

Dynamic pages ke liye generateMetadata() function — jo bhi data fetch karke uske hisaab se title/description lauta do.
lessons.analogy: Book ka cover page — andar ka content nahi hai, par shelf se uthane se pehle wahi sabse pehle dikhta hai. Metadata = aapke page ka cover, search results aur chat previews mein.
lessons.why: Pehle har page mein manually <Head> components likhne padte the — tags duplicate hote, miss hote. Metadata API ne ise ek export statement bana diya, aur duplicate tags apne aap merge ho gaye.

openGraph se WhatsApp/Twitter par sundar preview card.
pros: Declarative — tags likhna bhoolne ka sawaal hi nahi.
Parent-child metadata apne aap merge hota hai.
ImageResponse se OG images code se generate.
cons: Sirf Server Components mein kaam karta hai.
Har request par generateMetadata chalne se DB load.
OG image generation build time le sakti hai.
gotchas: Client component ('use client') se metadata export nahi kar sakte — build error.
generateMetadata aur page dono same data fetch karein to Request Memoization dedupe karti hai — double fetch mat likho.
Child page ka title parent ke template se guzarta hai — template lagana bhool jaao to titles flat dikhte hain.

lessons.name: Route Groups & Parallel Routes
lessons.desc: (group) syntax for organisation, @slot for parallel routes, conditional slot rendering
terms: Parentheses wala folder — organization ke liye, URL mein nahi aata.
Ek layout mein do-do pages saath render — named slots.
Slot ka fallback — jab refresh ke baad slot match na ho.
lessons.what:
(marketing)/about/page.tsx aur (shop)/cart/page.tsx — dono alag teams/alag layouts, par URL mein parentheses gayab: /about, /cart.

@modal, @stats jaise slots ek hi screen par kai independent pages render karte hain.
lessons.analogy: Society ke flats — building same, par A-wing/B-wing (groups) ka board gate par nahi dikhta. Parallel routes = ek TV par do windows split-screen — dono alag channel chala rahe.
lessons.why: Bade apps mein do problems hoti thin: (1) alag-alag layouts wale pages ka organization, (2) modal jaisi cheez URL ke saath sync rakhna. Groups ne organization di, parallel routes ne URL-driven modals ka clean tarika.

@modal slot + catch-all — modal URL se khulta/band hota hai, refresh par bhi tikta hai.
Independent widgets jo alag-alag load/stream hote hain.
pros: Same URL path par alag layouts — bina URL hack kiye.
Slots independently load/error ho sakte hain (apna loading.tsx).
Modal state URL mein — shareable links.
cons: Concept count badhta hai — naye dev confuse hote hain.
Do groups mein same path = build error, dhundhna padta hai.
Slots ke default.tsx likhna bhool jaate hain.
gotchas: Do route groups mein same page path mat do — (a)/about aur (b)/about conflict = build fail.
@slot ko layout mein render karna zaroori hai — props mein aayega, khud nahi dikhega.
Soft navigation ke baad direct refresh par slot match nahi hota to default.tsx chahiye hota hai — warna 404.

lessons.name: fetch() in Server Components
lessons.desc: Extending native fetch with {cache} and {next: {revalidate}} options in RSC. No useEffect needed.
terms: Server component ke andar seedha await fetch(...) — useEffect ki zarurat nahi.
Next.js ne native fetch ko patch kiya — cache/revalidate options diye.
Ek fetch khatam, tab doosra shuru — total time judta jaata hai.
lessons.what:
Server Components async ho sakte hain. Component ke andar seedha await karo — data HTML banne se pehle aa jaata hai.

Client-side jaisa useEffect + useState + loading spinner ka chakkar khatam.
lessons.analogy: Kitchen ka bawarchi khud bazaar jaakar sabzi laata hai, phir khana banata hai — plate (HTML) tabhi serve hoti jab khana ready ho. Waiter (useEffect) beech mein baar-baar nahi bhaagta.
lessons.why: Client-side fetching ka flow tha: khaali page → JS load → effect chala → spinner → data aaya → render. User ko dobara khaali screen dikhti thi. RSC mein data server par hi aata hai — pehli HTML hi poori aati hai.

visual.cap: Sequential await = waterfall (jodta gaya). Independent fetches ko Promise.all do — saath chalein.

where: Product detail, blog post, profile — sab RSC fetch se.
Secret keys server par rehti hain — client bundle mein nahi jaatin.
Prisma/Drisko direct await — fetch bhi zaroori nahi.
pros: Pehli HTML mein hi data — spinner ka daur khatam.
Secrets server par safe.
Database ke paas chalne se latency kam.
cons: Data aane tak poora block ho sakta hai — Suspense lagana zaroori.
Interactivity ke liye phir bhi Client Component chahiye.
fetch ke bahar (axios) wali libraries ko caching options nahi milte.
gotchas: Sequential awaits = waterfall — independent calls hamesha Promise.all mein. Interview ka favourite sawaal.
Ye sirf fetch par extend hota hai — Prisma/axios ko memoization/cache options nahi milte (React cache() alag se).
Server component mein browser APIs (window, localStorage) nahi chaltin — wo client-only hain.

lessons.name: Request Memoization
lessons.desc: Same fetch URL called multiple times in one render tree is deduped — automatic within a request lifecycle
terms: Ek render ke dauran same URL ka fetch ek hi baar hota hai — baaki cache se.
Functions ko per-request memoize karne ka React API — fetch ke bahar wali calls ke liye.
Ek HTTP request ka poora render tree — isi dauran memoization zinda hai.
lessons.what:
Layout, page, aur 3 components — sab getUser() bula rahe hain? Network par ek hi request jaayegi. Baaki sab ko wahi jawab milega.

Ye React ka cache() API hai jo Next ne fetch par apne aap laga diya.
lessons.analogy: Family mein 5 logon ne same pizza mangwaya — restaurant ne EK hi pizza banaya, sabko slice diye. Order (network call) ek baar, khana (data) sabko.
lessons.why: Nested layouts mein same data upar-neeche chahiye hota hai. Props neeche bhejna har jagah possible nahi. Memoization ne "props drilling ya duplicate fetch" ka dilemma khatam kiya — har jagah seedha fetch karo, dedupe framework karega.

visual.cap: Ek render tree, chaar jagah same fetch — network par sirf ek request gayi.

where: Header + page + sidebar sabko user chahiye — teen fetch, ek network call.
cache() wrap karke Prisma calls ko bhi dedupe karo.
"Same data multiple components mein kaise?" ka modern jawab.
pros: Code simple — har jagah seedha fetch, optimization framework ki.
Props drilling khatam.
Per-request scope — users ke beech data leak nahi hota.
cons: Sirf GET fetch auto-dedupe hota hai — POST/POST-like calls nahi.
Request khatam hote hi memoization clear — persistent cache NAHI hai.
Different URLs/headers = different cache keys, dedupe nahi hoga.
gotchas: Memoization ek request tak simit hai — agle visitor ke liye phir fetch hoga. Persistent chahiye to Data Cache dekho.
cache() sirf server par kaam karta hai — client components mein nahi.
Cookies/headers padhne wale fetch dedupe nahi hote — har call unique hoti hai.

lessons.name: Data Cache
lessons.desc: Persistent across requests and deployments. force-cache (default), no-store, revalidate: N
terms: Server-side persistent cache — requests aur deployments ke beech bhi zinda.
Data ko cache karo (purani default behaviour).
Har request par fresh data — cache mat karo.
lessons.what:
Data Cache build/deploy se bhi lambi zindagi wala cache hai. Ek user ke liye fetch hua data agle visitors ko bhi wahi cached milega (jab tak revalidate na ho).

Control: fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 60 } }) — 60 second tak cached.
lessons.analogy: Fridge — bazaar (origin server) har baar nahi jaana. Ek baar grocery laayo, fridge se kaam chalao. Har ghante (revalidate) mein taaza doodh check karne ka alarm laga do.
lessons.why: Har visitor par origin server + DB ko hit karna mehnga aur slow hai. Data Cache se 1000 visitors = 1 DB query (jab tak fresh nahi karo). Ye CDN-level speed data par bhi deta hai.

visual.cap: Pehli request: miss → origin → cache mein save. Agle sab: hit → turant jawab.

where: Blog posts, products, prices — sab cache-worthy.
Cart, profile — no-store ya cookies-based dynamic rendering.
pros: DB/API load dramatically kam.
Response times near-instant.
Tags se surgical invalidation.
cons: Stale data dikh sakta hai — strategy soch samajh kar.
Galat cheez cache = sab users ko galat data.
Debugging tough — "data kahan se aaya?" ka jawab layers mein hai.
gotchas: Next.js 15 mein default no-store ho gaya — 14 wale tutorials ka "fetch by default cached" ab galat hai.
Cookies/headers padhne wale fetches cache nahi hote — personalized data ke liye yahi sahi hai.
revalidate: 60 ka matlab "har 60s par refresh" nahi — "60s ke baad PEHLI request par background refresh".

lessons.name: Full Route Cache
lessons.desc: Cached HTML + RSC payload at build time for static routes. Invalidated by revalidatePath/revalidateTag
terms: Static routes ka rendered HTML + RSC payload build time par ban kar ready.
Koi dynamic API (cookies, searchParams) use hui to route dynamic — cache nahi hota.
revalidatePath/Tag se cached route delete, agli request par fresh.
lessons.what:
Agar route mein koi dynamic cheez nahi hai, to Next build time par poora HTML bana kar rakh leta hai. Har visitor ko wahi ready-made HTML CDNs se milta hai — server chalta hi nahi.

Ek bhi cookies()/headers()/searchParams use hua → route dynamic → har request par render.
lessons.analogy: Pre-printed pamphlet — printing press (build) mein ek baar chap gaya, ab lakhs copies seedha baant do. Customized letter (dynamic) chahiye to har baar likhna padega.
lessons.why: Static HTML serve karna sabse tez aur sasta hai — server CPU zero, TTFB near-zero. Full Route Cache ka goal: zyada se zyada routes static rahen, sirf zaroori hisse dynamic.

where: Landing, pricing, about — sab static, lightning fast.
Posts build par static, revalidate se fresh.
Personalized data = dynamic — yahan cache expect mat karo.
pros: Sabse tez possible delivery — pre-built HTML.
Server cost almost zero for static routes.
SEO perfect — poora HTML pehli response mein.
cons: Build time badh jaata hai — hazaron routes = lambi builds.
Anjaane mein dynamic API use kar lena route ko dynamic kar deta hai.
Content update ke liye revalidation chahiye.
gotchas: searchParams use karte hi route dynamic ho jaata hai — build output mein tick/cross symbols check karo.
Router Cache (client) alag cheez hai — Full Route Cache server-side hai, dono ko mix mat karo.
revalidatePath('/blog') sirf us route ka cache todta hai — Data Cache bhi saath mein invalidate hota hai agar linked hai.

lessons.name: Router Cache (Client)
lessons.desc: Client-side cache of visited route segments. Prefetched on hover. Duration: 30s (dynamic), 5min (static)
terms: Browser (client) mein visited routes ke RSC payloads ki memory.
<Link> viewport/hover par route ka payload pehle se laa leta hai.
Server se current route ka fresh data mangwata hai — cache refresh.
lessons.what:
Jab aap kisi route par jaate ho, uska RSC payload browser memory mein save ho jaata hai. Wapas wahi route par jaoge to network call hi nahi hogi — instant navigation.

<Link> prefetch karta hai: static routes full payload, dynamic routes sirf loading skeleton.
lessons.analogy: Roz ka rasta — pehli baar GPS chahiye, uske baad yaad ho jaata hai. Ghar se office (back navigation) ab bina soche pahunch jaate ho. Prefetch = kal ke meeting ka venue aaj hi dekh lena.
lessons.why: Har click par server round-trip hota to SPA feel nahi aati. Router Cache ne client-side instant navigation diya — bina poora app client bundle mein laaye.

visual.cap: Hover/viewport par prefetch → click par instant. Back/forward cache se bilkul free.

where: SPA-jaisa smooth — bina SPA bundle ke.
router.refresh() se UI server state se sync.
cons: Stale data 30s/5min tak dikh sakta hai.
Cache DevTools mein nahi dikhta — debugging andhera.
Bahut saare Links = bahut prefetch requests.
gotchas: Router Cache memory-only hai — page refresh karte hi saaf.
Dynamic routes ka prefetch sirf partial hota hai (shared layout tak) — poora payload nahi.
Mutation ke baad list update na ho to router.refresh() bhool gaye ho — classic bug.

lessons.name: Revalidation Strategies
lessons.desc: Time-based (revalidate: N), on-demand (revalidatePath, revalidateTag), tags with fetch cache tags
terms: revalidate: N — N seconds baad cache "stale", agli request par refresh.
Fetch par tag laga do, baad mein us naam se poora group invalidate.
lessons.what:
Cached data ko fresh karne ke do tarike: time-based ("60 sec baad stale maano") aur on-demand ("post publish hui? abhi revalidate karo").

On-demand precise hota hai — poora site nahi, sirf related cache tootta hai.
lessons.analogy: Doodh packet par expiry date (time-based) — date nikli to naya lao. Aur jab dukaandar bole "aaj ka fresh aaya hai" (on-demand) — tab bhi purana phenk kar naya lo. Dono ka apna jagah hai.
lessons.why: Sirf time-based revalidation ka problem: content turant update karna ho to max 60s wait. Sirf on-demand: har chhoti cheez ke liye webhook likhna padega. Real apps dono use karti hain.

visual.cap: Time-based: expiry ke baad pehli request stale deti hai, background refresh. On-demand: publish hote hi turant.

where: Stock/price change par sirf product pages fresh.
Action ke saath revalidatePath — UI turant sync.
pros: Fresh jab zaroori, cached jab possible — best of both.
Tags se grouped invalidation — ek shot mein related sab.
User-facing updates instant.
cons: Kaunsa tag/path revalidate karna hai, yaad rakhna padta hai.
Galat tag = cache kabhi nahi tootta ya galat tootta hai.
Sirf server context mein call ho sakta hai (actions/handlers).
gotchas: revalidateTag Data Cache tootta hai, lekin client ka Router Cache nahi — uske liye router.refresh() bhi chahiye.
revalidatePath('/') sirf exact / tootta hai — sab kuch nahi. Sab ke liye revalidatePath('/', 'layout').
Time-based revalidation stale-while-revalidate hai — expiry ke turant baad bhi PEHLI request purana deti hai.

lessons.name: RSC vs Client Components
lessons.desc: "use client" creates a boundary. RSC: no hooks, no events, can async/await, runs on server only

lessons.name: Composition Patterns
lessons.desc: Passing RSC as children to Client Components. Server-only imports. The "leaves are clients" principle.

lessons.name: Streaming with Suspense
lessons.desc: <Suspense> boundaries enable streaming HTML. loading.tsx as implicit Suspense. Manual Suspense for granular control.

lessons.name: Server Actions
lessons.desc: "use server" directive. Form action={action}. useFormState, useFormStatus. Progressive enhancement.

lessons.name: Optimistic UI
